articles.title: You need to listen to the brutally oppressive I’ve Seen All I Need to See
articles.summary: The Body’s 2021 record sounds like being buried alive.
articles.body: There are only a handful of albums that I think qualify as genuinely scary. You Won’t Get What You Want by Daughters, and Swans To Be Kind both immediately come to mind. But those records come with… let’s say, baggage. I’ve Seen All I Need to See lacks some of the atmospheric spookiness of To Be Kind and the flashes of pop-tinged menace of You Won’t Get What You Want, but it makes up for that with unrelenting brutality. It’s not the soundtrack to a slasher film, it’s the most violent scene in the bleakest horror film, rendered as blown-out drums and detuned guitar. The album opens with a reading of Douglas Dunn’s The Kaleidoscope, a poem about being trapped in a cycle of grief, as sparse drums boom arhythmically alongside bursts of noise and a low metallic drone. As it transitions into the distant shriek of vocalist / guitarist Chip King, “A Lament” sputters in fits and starts as it struggles to take flight. That sets the tone for the record, which is less a collection of songs and more a relentless monolith erected in tribute to the power of distortion. And this is where I admit, I’ve Seen All I Need to See won’t be for everyone. It’s largely atonal, tracks can blend into each other, and even when the drums pick the pace up beyond funeral dirge, the songs feel weighed down, like the band is trying to play their way out of a bog. That’s not to say there aren’t moments of catharsis to be found. The City is Shelled in particular, erupts towards its back end as King’s vocals become a Goblin-esque croak over pounding piano chords, delivering one of the few moments of genuine melodicism (even if it’s buried under a skyscraper of fuzz). Even though it’s only 38 minutes long, at times, I’ve Seen All I Need to See can feel like an endurance exercise. But, like a marathon, that doesn’t mean it’s not worth enduring. There is beauty in its brutality. It’s haunting and vicious in the way that, say, Bring Her Back is. Good art is not necessarily pleasant art. If you’re looking for a record that conjures horror movie vibes without devolving into camp. Something that feels genuinely dangerous and frightening, and not just merely kind of spooky, The Body’s I’ve Seen All I Need to See is what you’re looking for. articles.title: 1º Festival do Mel tem rodeio, concurso e música ao vivo no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento iniciou nesta quinta-feira (5) e segue até domingo (8) no Centro do Bujari. Iniciativa busca valorizar a apicultura, incentivar o empreendedorismo e fortalecer a economia local.
articles.summary: Evento iniciou nesta quinta-feira (5) e segue até domingo (8) no Centro do Bujari. Iniciativa busca valorizar a apicultura, incentivar o empreendedorismo e fortalecer a economia.
articles.body:
Entre esta quinta-feira (5) e domingo (8) ocorre o 1º Festival do Mel no município do Bujari, interior do Acre, com diversas atrações musicais, concurso do melhor produtor de mel, rodeio, escolha da Garota Mel e concurso da Rainha, Princesa e Madrinha do Rodeio.

A iniciativa foi criada para valorizar a produção de mel, incentivar o empreendedorismo e fortalecer a economia local. A Rede Amazônica Acre é parceira do evento.

A festividade tem ainda o objetivo de valorizar a apicultura e os produtores locais, incentivando o empreendedorismo e criando oportunidades para a venda de produtos.

Além disso, o evento pretende destacar o potencial econômico e cultural do município. A abertura do festival ocorreu às 17h em uma estrutura montada no Centro do município, na Avenida José Pereira Gurgel.

O público pode aproveitar as barracas com venda de comida e lanches, parques e brinquedos para as crianças e expositores com produções locais.

articles.title: Fesmorena 2026: júri se reúne para escolher 22 finalistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Festival recebeu mais de 200 inscrições de estudantes de Mato Grosso do Sul e Mato Grosso. A grande final acontece em dezembro, no Teatro Dom Bosco, com entrada gratuita.
articles.summary: Festival recebeu mais de 200 inscrições de estudantes de Mato Grosso do Sul e Mato Grosso. A grande final acontece em dezembro, no Teatro Dom Bosco, com entrada gratuita.
articles.body:
A banca de jurados do 11º Festival de Música Autoral Estudantil (Fesmorena) escolheu, na tarde desta quinta-feira (5), os 22 finalistas da edição de 2026. A seleção ocorreu na sede da TV Morena, em Campo Grande, e definiu os estudantes que vão disputar a grande final nas categorias Música Autoral Livre e Canção "50 Anos de MS".

O festival recebeu 237 inscrições de estudantes de 7 a 17 anos de Mato Grosso do Sul e Mato Grosso. Das 22 vagas na final, 15 são destinadas à categoria Música Autoral Livre e sete à Canção "50 Anos de MS".

Antes da reunião, os jurados avaliaram as músicas individualmente. No encontro, eles reuniram os resultados e confirmaram as composições selecionadas para a final.

As músicas inscritas abordam temas do cotidiano de crianças e adolescentes, como primeiros amores, saudade, lembranças da infância e relações familiares.

Também há composições sobre a preservação do Pantanal, espiritualidade, autoestima, desigualdade, violência e os impactos das telas nas relações sociais.

Outras canções valorizam as tradições culturais de Mato Grosso do Sul, homenageiam artistas regionais e usam o humor para retratar a identidade dos dois estados.

A banca de jurados foi formada pelos cantores e compositores Victor Gregório, Dora Sanches, Marco Aurélio e Pescuma; pelas cantoras Juno e Ana Gaborim, que também é doutora em Música; e pelo músico e doutor em Música Marcelo Fernandes.

Também participaram da seleção o historiador e crítico cultural Raul Ruffo e as jornalistas e apresentadoras Bruna Mendes e Lucimar Lescano.

As músicas foram avaliadas conforme os critérios previstos no regulamento do festival.

Os 22 finalistas terão acesso a atividades de preparação, com orientações sobre presença de palco, canto e afinação vocal.

Uma das novidades desta edição é a categoria Canção "50 Anos de MS", criada para incentivar estudantes a compor músicas sobre a história, as tradições e a identidade de Mato Grosso do Sul.

A iniciativa faz parte da preparação para os 50 anos de criação do estado, comemorados em 2027.

O Fesmorena está na 11ª edição e busca incentivar a criação de músicas autorais e revelar novos talentos entre crianças e adolescentes.

O festival é realizado pelo Instituto Cerrado Central (ICC), com recursos do governo federal, por meio do Ministério da Cultura.

A grande final será realizada no dia 20 de dezembro, às 18h, no Teatro Dom Bosco, em Campo Grande. A entrada será gratuita.

articles.title: El Gran Wyoming se jubila y deja 'El Intermedio' tras 20 años: Gonzo será su presentador desde enero
articles.standfirst: La Sexta se prepara para la salida de una de las figuras más visibles de su programación
articles.summary: La Sexta se prepara para la salida de una de las figuras más visibles de su programación
articles.body: El Gran Wyoming se jubila. El mítico presentador de 'El Intermedio', programa de La Sexta que ha dirigido durante los últimos 20 años, vivirá sus últimas semanas conduciendo el programa en solitario para poner punto y final a una carrera longeva en la televisión a sus 71 años. Su sustituto en el programa será una vieja cara reconocida por los espectadores como Gonzo, que dejará el programa de 'Salvados' para presentar 'El Intermedio', como ha adelantado El País. Un relevo que será progresivo y desde enero, por tiempo indefinido, compartirán la dirección del programa hasta que su heredero tome el control del programa de forma definitiva. José Miguel Monzón Navarro, mundialmente conocido como El Gran Wyoming, es una de las figuras más polifacéticas e influyentes de la comunicación y la cultura popular en España. Médico de formación pero humorista, músico y actor de vocación, dio sus primeros pasos artísticos en la década de 1970 vinculado a la contracultura madrileña y al rock. Su mordacidad natural y su estilo corrosivo pronto lo convirtieron en un rostro habitual del espectáculo, dando el salto a los medios masivos donde consagraría una personalidad mediática caracterizada por la ironía, el compromiso político y una absoluta falta de reverencia hacia el poder. Su andadura televisiva despegó en los años 80 y 90 con espacios de culto como La noche se mueve o El peor programa del mundo, donde empezó a moldear su perfil de presentador irreverente. Sin embargo, el verdadero hito que revolucionó el formato del late night en España fue Caiga Quien Caiga (CQC) en Telecinco a finales de los noventa. Vestido con su icónico traje negro y rodeado de un equipo de reporteros punzantes, Wyoming convirtió la sátira política y la crítica al periodismo tradicional en un fenómeno de audiencia que marcó a toda una generación. Desde 2006, su figura ha quedado indisolublemente ligada a la historia de laSexta como rostro titular de El Intermedio. Durante dos décadas al frente del espacio con la célebre muletilla "ya conocen las noticias, ahora les contaremos la verdad", ha consolidado un formato de análisis de actualidad basado en el humor ácido y la denuncia social. Convertido en el decano de la sátira informativa en la televisión española, Wyoming ha sabido mantener intacta su vigencia combinando el rigor del guión periodístico con su inconfundible vis cómica.

articles.title: ‘Married At First Sight UK’ dropped by network after women say they were raped during show
articles.summary: The U.K. version of the “Married At First Sight” reality franchise has canceled its season after allegations that two women were raped during the production of the show.
articles.body: The U.K. version of the “Married At First Sight” reality franchise will no longer air on Channel 4 after allegations that two women were raped during the production of the show. Channel 4 chief executive Priya Dogra confirmed in a statement Thursday the network was cutting ties with the reality series following an external review of the allegations made while filming its sixth season. The review found no wrongdoing by the network or the show’s production company, CPL, but Dogra said that the “right course was to bring Married At First Sight UK on Channel 4 to an end.” “Whilst the review praised the welfare protocols in place and made no findings that ... the format is inherently unsafe, I have to consider when is the right time for Channel 4 to move on from a format,” Dogra said. The rape allegations were first revealed this summer in a BBC Panorama investigation. One of the two women alleged that the husband she was matched with raped her and threatened her with an acid attack, according to the BBC. A third woman accused her onscreen husband of sexual misconduct. All three men involved denied the allegations. The premise of “Married At First Sight” is that a group of contestants agree to be matched with complete strangers and meet at the altar. Couples are then followed by the cameras as they navigate their relationship and discuss their problems on air with the show’s counselors. Version of the show have aired across the world, including the U.S., Australia, France, and Spain. Channel 4 hired a law firm to review safety protocols at the time of the alleged sexual misconduct and how the production company handled them once they were raised, the company said in a press release. The network’s review did not seek “to adjudicate” the allegations, which it said “remain a matter for the relevant authorities.” More than 30,000 documents were reviewed by law firm Clyde & Co in addition to hours of footage, according to Channel 4. The review found that the production company and network were compliant with regulations from the U.K.’s Office of Communications. A full version of the review was not made available but Channel 4 did provide a summary of findings, noting that the report was a “legally privileged and confidential review.” There was no overall breach of the broadcasting code, though the full “welfare framework” was not applied in some incidents, the review found. One of the incidents included contributors who broke rules regarding “prohibited substances” but were given a warning rather than being removed. A report from former BBC One controller Lorraine Heggessey, who was asked to examine if any protocols should be changed, said that there are elements of the show that could put pressure on individuals to be physically intimate. She recommended that the show consider discontinuing events such as Intimacy Week and Partner Swap Week. Heggessey’s report said that the show’s stars could “become dependent on production and lose touch with reality,” which could affect decision-making. She also recommended the show consider changing the mechanism in place that forces a couple to remain for another week if one person in a couple wants to leave but the other asks to stay during their weekly commitment ceremonies. Among some of the recommendations were to install video and recording equipment in couple’s apartments to be monitored 24/7, provide couple’s separate bedrooms, provide “panic buttons,” and allow contributors to have at least one unsupervised visit back home during production. The network said the full implementation of the recommendations “would entail a materially greater level of intervention, monitoring and supervision that would fundamentally alter the format and editorial proposition of the programme.” “The recommendations are eminently sensible and feasible, but considering their wholesale implementation provoked fundamental questions about the editorial proposition of a show that, I believe, has now run its course over ten years,” Dogra said. Dogra said that the money budgeted for the series would be reinvested into finding “the next generation of distinctive and disruptive British television.” She thanked the staff who worked on the series and credited them for their “significant efforts to protect the welfare of contributors.” The production company, CPL, said it understood Channel 4’s decision to part ways with the reality program, according to Sky News. It emphasized in its statement that Heggessey’s report found the welfare protocols to be “extensive, extremely thorough and of a high standard.” “CPL has always put contributor welfare at the heart of its programme making and will continue to do so,” the company said. This is not the franchise’s first controversy. The show’s Australia series has been criticized for subjecting contestants to potentially harmful situations, including a man who had a history of domestic abuse allegations. While the allegations were dismissed before filming began, the woman who was matched with him told The Guardian in June that the show “obviously needed a better vetting process.” “We are strangers sleeping in a bedroom on our own on the first night, you’ve got no security, you’re by yourselves,” Awhina Rutene told the outlet. She added that she was not subjected to abuse, but noted that the environment felt invasive and that physical intimacy felt “forced.” “Every morning (in interviews) they’d be like, ‘Why aren’t you having sex?’” Rutene said. The Australian Communications and Media Authority has conducted 10 investigations, according to the Guardian, and no breaches of its code of practice were found. If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. The hotline, run by the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN), can put you in contact with your local rape crisis center. You can also access RAINN’s online chat service at Confidential chats are available in English and in Spanish.

articles.title: The Met’s Costume Institute reveals new exhibit after axing controversial Galliano show
articles.summary: A new theme for next year’s Met Gala exhibit was announced Thursday, two months after event organizers scrapped their original idea to honor British designer John Galliano following backlash over his past anti-Jewish and anti-Asian remarks.
articles.body: A new theme for next year’s Met Gala exhibit was announced Thursday, two months after event organizers scrapped their original idea to honor British designer John Galliano following backlash over his past anti-Jewish and anti-Asian remarks. The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York City, which hosts the annual star-studded event commonly known as fashion’s biggest night, said the replacement exhibit will examine how fashion designers transform conventional objects and everyday clothing to create new garments. “From jeans, T-shirts, and puffer coats to paper, plastic, and metal, the exhibition will reveal how the seemingly unremarkable can inspire delight, surprise, and wonder,” the museum said in a press release Thursday. “The exhibition will examine how craft, construction, material experimentation, and conceptual wit give these ordinary forms extraordinary possibilities.” Titled “extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday,” the exhibit is being assembled by the Met’s Costume Institute, which curates the exhibit and theme of the Met Gala, an annual fundraiser for the institute. The exhibit’s theme typically determines the dress code for the Met Gala, which traditionally falls on the first Monday in May. Andrew Bolton, head curator at the Costume Institute, spoke to The Associated Press this week about the challenges he faced coming up with a new idea following the cancellation of the Galliano show. “I had no Plan B, to be honest,” Bolton said. “There wasn’t another exhibition already researched and ready to go.” With little time to come up with a new idea, Bolton said he relied on a passing thought he had while working on the last Met Gala exhibition, which explored the relationship different types of bodies have with clothing. That previous show “sort of led me to think more about how we experience clothing in everyday life,” Bolton said. “We have a favorite T-shirt, we have a favorite pair of jeans, and we wear them until they literally fall apart.” “Everyday clothes carry extraordinary amounts of meaning,” he added. “I like the idea that designers turn these familiar things into these incredible sources of wonder.” Before changing course, the Costume Institute had already been collecting Galliano designs for the original show, which was announced in late July. As controversy ensued, the museum said it would not shy away from confronting the designer’s “derogatory conduct that fundamentally altered his career and public reception,” but the exhibit in his honor was ultimately canceled in August. At the time, museum director Max Hollein said the institution and Galliano decided together not to proceed with the original show. The influential Galliano spent years as the creative director of Christian Dior. He was fired in 2011 over a series of racist and antisemitic comments that went viral online. That same year, the designer was convicted of antisemitic abuse in France after berating a couple at a cafe in Paris. Galliano blamed the behavior on substance abuse and testified in court that he had no recollection of the events. Galliano later made a comeback in 2014 when he was hired by Paris fashion house Maison Margiela, where he remained for a decade. If left unchanged, the unveiling of the Galliano exhibit would have coincided with Holocaust Remembrance Day on May 3, 2027. Longtime Met Gala chair Anna Wintour, who is also Vogue’s global editorial director and a longtime supporter of Galliano, supported Hollein’s and Galliano’s joint decision to cancel the show. “John’s decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is,” Wintour said in an August statement. “I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support.”

articles.title: La piña en la pizza le cuesta el puesto a un chef italiano en Australia: "Es un insulto a mi cultura"
articles.standfirst: Davide Tamburella fue despedido de un restaurante de Brisbane tras negarse a preparar pizzas de jamón y piña para un evento privado
articles.summary: Davide Tamburella fue despedido de un restaurante de Brisbane tras negarse a preparar pizzas de jamón y piña para un evento privado
articles.body: Un cocinero italiano ha perdido su trabajo en Australia después de negarse a preparar pizzas con piña por considerar que incluir esta fruta en la receta suponía un "insulto" a su cultura. Davide Tamburella fue despedido el pasado mes de mayo del restaurante 'La Costa', en Brisbane, después de rechazar la petición de elaborar pizzas de jamón y piña para los asistentes a un evento privado. El caso ha trascendido ahora después de que el chef italiano acudiera a la Comisión de Trabajo Justo de Australia (Fair Work Commission) para denunciar que su despido había sido improcedente. Sin embargo, el organismo ha rechazado su solicitud al considerar que la reclamación se presentó fuera del plazo establecido por la legislación australiana, por lo que no ha llegado a pronunciarse sobre el fondo de la cuestión. La resolución recoge, además, que el enfrentamiento por la piña no fue un episodio aislado y que la dirección del establecimiento tenía otras preocupaciones relacionadas con el comportamiento y la actitud del cocinero. El incidente que desencadenó el despido se produjo durante un evento privado celebrado en mayo. El organizador había contratado un servicio gastronómico valorado en más de 15.000 dólares australianos y había solicitado expresamente pizzas de jamón y piña. Davide Tamburella se negó a prepararlas y defendió que no tenía por qué seguir las instrucciones de la gerencia cuando consideraba que eran ofensivas para su cultura. Según recoge la resolución de la Comisión de Trabajo Justo, era la tercera vez en los últimos cuatro años que el chef se negaba a utilizar piña en una pizza. En una de las ocasiones anteriores, había pedido reiteradamente a su superior que comprobara "lo importante que es para los italianos no poner piña en la pizza". La dirección del restaurante mantuvo una reunión con él unas dos semanas antes de despedirlo, en la que le trasladó distintas quejas sobre su comportamiento. Las objeciones de la empresa no se limitaban a sus discrepancias gastronómicas. También hacían referencia al lenguaje soez que utilizaba, a su estilo de comunicación y a lo que describieron como una "escalada de la frustración en el lugar de trabajo". El director general del restaurante, Elliot Ingram, aseguró que la historia "era más compleja que un simple ingrediente de pizza". El responsable reconoció que tampoco le gustaba especialmente la pizza con piña, pero defendió que "hay que saber elegir las batallas". La resolución recoge asimismo un accidente laboral sufrido por Davide Tamburella el pasado mes de abril, cuando se fracturó varios huesos de la mano derecha al golpearse contra una barandilla metálica. El caso tiene también una dimensión laboral y personal. El cocinero esperaba que el restaurante patrocinara su visado para poder acceder a la residencia permanente en Australia a través de un programa dirigido a trabajadores cualificados. Después de su despido, el establecimiento interrumpió los trámites para esa solicitud. La polémica adquiere un matiz especialmente llamativo por el lugar en el que se produjo. Queensland, el estado australiano donde se encuentra Brisbane, es el principal territorio productor de piña del país y concentra toda su producción comercial. Allí se encuentra también 'The Big Pineapple', una réplica de fibra de vidrio de 16 metros de altura dedicada a esta fruta y convertida en uno de los puntos de referencia de la zona. Después de abandonar 'La Costa', Davide Tamburella comenzó a trabajar en otro restaurante de Brisbane, según indica su perfil de LinkedIn. En esa misma plataforma se presenta como un profesional centrado en ofrecer una comida excepcional y mejorar el rendimiento de los negocios hosteleros. Hace tres meses publicó, además, una carta dirigida a otros cocineros bajo el lema "respetar los ingredientes". Una investigación periodística sobre su nuevo lugar de trabajo constató que la piña no figura en la carta del establecimiento.

articles.title: After the John Galliano fallout, the 2027 Met Gala theme is going back to basics
articles.summary: After canceling its controversial John Galliano exhibition, the Met has announced a new theme celebrating the extraordinary potential of ordinary clothes. Th...
articles.body:
The Metropolitan Museum of Art announced on Thursday that the theme of its spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition will be "extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday," which will explore how designers transform wardrobe staples and commonplace materials into something remarkable. Think jeans, T-shirts and puffer coats, alongside creations incorporating paper, plastic and metal.

The announcement comes just over two months after the museum canceled its planned exhibition honoring John Galliano . First announced in July, "John Galliano: Horizons" was intended to examine the designer's decades-long career, from his early collections to his work at Givenchy, Christian Dior and Maison Margiela. But the planned exhibition was met with backlash over the designer's past antisemitic and racist remarks, which led to his dismissal from Dior and his 2011 conviction of making "public insults" based on race, religion, ethnicity or origin following two incidents at a Paris bar. Although the museum said it would confront that conduct in the exhibition, the prospect of honoring Galliano still drew criticism from Jewish community members, donors and public officials .

The timing added to the controversy: The 2027 gala, taking place on the first Monday in May, as always, falls on Israel's Holocaust Remembrance Day. On Aug. 31, the museum and Galliano announced that the exhibition would not proceed.

That left the Costume Institute with a major opening in its calendar, and little time to fill it.

"I didn't have a plan B," Andrew Bolton, the curator in charge, told Vogue , adding that it was important "to come up with an idea that wasn't a substitute" for the Galliano show. Inspiration came from the 2026 exhibition's theme of "Costume Art."

"I suppose it led me to think more about how we experience clothing in everyday life through habit and touch and movement and sensation," said Bolton.

According to the New York Times , the exhibition will feature 200 to 230 pieces. Among them: Charles James's couture take on a puffer coat from the 1930s, designs from Marc Jacobs's 1990s grunge collection for Perry Ellis and the Calvin Klein jeans Brooke Shields wore in her famous ad .

Does that mean celebrities will trade elaborate gowns for jeans on the Met steps? That remains to be seen — the gala's dress code has yet to be announced.

And while Galliano's exhibition is off, whether his designs will appear on the carpet is another question. After all, his Met Gala history spans decades , from dressing Princess Diana in 1996 to designing looks for Kim Kardashian in 2024 and Stevie Nicks in 2026.

articles.title: María Patiño cuenta el desplante que sufrió de Georgina Rodríguez y desvela el motivo detrás de su actitud: "Me dio la espalda"
articles.standfirst: La televisiva desvela una situación vivida con la pareja de Cristiano Ronaldo en un evento
articles.summary: La televisiva desvela una situación vivida con la pareja de Cristiano Ronaldo en un evento
articles.body: Tras varios días como nueva presentadora de ‘El Sótano Queen’, en TEN, tras la salida de Alba Carrillo rumbo a La Séptima, María Patiño ha sacado a escena un desplante que sufrió por parte de Georgina Rodríguez. La televisiva, en sus primeras entregas al frente del programa, reveló la situación a la que se tuvo que enfrentar con la pareja de Cristiano Ronaldo. Tuvo lugar en un evento corporativo en el que estuvieron cara a cara. Patiño, en su regreso a la televisión varios meses después, confesó que no dudó en que Georgina Rodríguez la vio, pero que optó por no presentarse: “No me quiso conocer y me dio la espalda, o sea, se giró”, afirmó en referencia a este preciso instante. Sin embargo, más allá de esta situación incómoda con la mujer del futbolista portugués, la información que le llega de ella es muy positiva: “La verdad es que me han hablado muy bien de ella. En el documental que hizo con Netflix el equipo decía que era supergenerosa y que regalaba de todo a la gente”. En este contexto, la conductora de ‘El Sótano Queen’ llegó a plantear la hipótesis de que si esta actitud de Georgina Rodríguez era porque le conocía o algo similar: “A lo mejor es que le caigo mal”, apuntó. Eso sí, por último, desveló la explicación que recibió de una fuente directa del entorno de la mujer del que fuera jugador del Real Madrid que despejó todas sus dudas de un plumazo: “Me escribió la gente de su equipo y me dijeron que fue una decisión de su equipo y no de ella”, sentenció María Patiño visiblemente calmada tras explicar este encuentro con Georgina Rodríguez de años atrás.

articles.title: Rodrigo de la Calle propone nuevas formas de disfrutar y cocinar con caviar
articles.standfirst: Caviar Riofrío y el chef madrileño proponen una experiencia gastronómica participativa para descubrir nuevas aplicaciones de este producto
articles.summary: Caviar Riofrío y el chef madrileño proponen una experiencia gastronómica participativa para descubrir nuevas aplicaciones de este producto
articles.body: El caviar se puede disfrutar de muchas más formas de las que dicta la tradición. Con esta premisa, Caviar Riofrío y el chef Rodrigo de la Calle, al frente del restaurante 'El Invernadero', han diseñado una experiencia gastronómica que combina cocina en directo, aprendizaje y degustación. Se trata de un exclusivo menú-taller de nueve pases en el que los asistentes no solo probarán diferentes elaboraciones con caviar, sino que también participarán en la preparación de algunos platos y aprenderán técnicas para reproducirlas en casa. La propuesta, concebida para disfrutar de una experiencia diferente esta Navidad, se desarrollará en la mesa del chef de 'El Invernadero', restaurante reconocido con una Estrella Michelin y una Estrella Verde Michelin. Cada sesión tendrá una duración aproximada de dos horas y media y estará limitada a un máximo de diez participantes, lo que permitirá mantener un formato cercano y participativo. Durante el encuentro, Rodrigo de la Calle explicará las distintas posibilidades culinarias del caviar, desde su utilización en fresco como aderezo hasta su aplicación en elaboraciones a la brasa o su transformación en sal y mantequilla. También mostrará cómo incorporarlo a vinagretas, escabeches e incluso postres. Además, los asistentes intervendrán directamente en la finalización de cuatro platos: el cogollo de Tudela, el mollete de trufa negra, el esturión ecológico en escabeche y el steak tartar. "Me gustaría que se vayan con ideas que puedan repetir en casa, como la mantequilla de caviar, y con la sensación de haber cocinado conmigo en un formato cercano, con la cocina abierta delante", explica el chef. El menú comienza con una panacota de almendras con caviar Riofrío y caqui, una propuesta que juega con la apariencia de un postre y el contraste salino del producto. A continuación, llegan un cogollo de Tudela al wok con vinagreta de caviar y un nigiri vegetal de pimiento rojo asado. El recorrido continúa con un mollete de trufa negra con mantequilla y sal de caviar, seguido de una coliflor cremosa con navajas y caviar a la brasa, que incorpora matices ahumados. El pez limón en tempura con salsa de ajo y jengibre introduce nuevas combinaciones de sabores, mientras que el esturión ecológico en escabeche de caviar y el steak tartar de ternera blanca de la sierra de Guadarrama con sal de caviar muestran otras formas de integrar este ingrediente en la cocina salada. El menú concluye con una elaboración de queso, remolacha, trufa y caviar, que lleva el producto al terreno dulce. Cada pase cuenta con una propuesta de maridaje seleccionada para acompañar sus sabores, con referencias como la cerveza de algas Albeer, Montecillo Blanco Fermentado en Barrica, La Honda con Fino y Amontillado en Rama, de Osborne, y el tinto Viña Monty Graciano. La experiencia termina con un dulce casero de almendras elaborado en el restaurante. La colaboración entre Caviar Riofrío y Rodrigo de la Calle también responde a una filosofía compartida en torno a la sostenibilidad y el aprovechamiento integral de los ingredientes. El chef, referente de la cocina vegetal en España y pionero en el desarrollo de la gastrobotánica y la revolución verde, concede un papel protagonista a las verduras, mientras que los productos de origen animal acompañan las elaboraciones. "En 'El Invernadero' la verdura manda y el producto animal acompaña. Para mí, el respeto al producto es aprovecharlo entero: del esturión usamos el caviar, la sal de caviar, la mantequilla y también el lomo, que va en un escabeche. Eso es respetar el origen y cocinar con sentido", destaca el chef. Esta apuesta por el aprovechamiento y la producción responsable conecta con la trayectoria de Caviar Riofrío, que en 2001 se convirtió en el primer productor de caviar del mundo en obtener la certificación ecológica. La compañía desarrolla su actividad en la Sierra de Loja, en Granada, donde cría esturiones en aguas de manantial y controla todo el proceso, desde la cría hasta la obtención del caviar, mediante un modelo conocido como 'egg to egg'. Su sistema de producción prioriza la trazabilidad, el bienestar animal y el respeto por los ciclos naturales de los esturiones. Algunas especies, como el Acipenser naccarii, pueden necesitar hasta 18 años para producir su primer caviar. La marca mantiene así su compromiso con la producción artesanal y sostenible y se ha convertido también en el primer productor de caviar Beluga ecológico en España. Las sesiones del menú-taller tendrán lugar los viernes 20 y 27 de noviembre y 4 y 11 de diciembre, a las 14.00 horas, en 'El Invernadero'. Cada encuentro contará con un máximo de diez asistentes y requerirá un mínimo de seis participantes para celebrarse. Los interesados podrán elegir entre dos modalidades: el menú de nueve pases, con un precio de 125 euros por persona, o la experiencia completa con maridaje, infusiones, café y otros acompañamientos, por 175 euros por persona. Una iniciativa que busca demostrar que el caviar puede ser mucho más que un producto reservado para grandes celebraciones y que también tiene cabida en recetas creativas, accesibles y reproducibles en la cocina doméstica.

articles.title: Matt Damon shares update on wife Luciana's health after brain aneurysm surgery
articles.summary: The actor said his wife, Luciana, had surgery just a week before the Oscars.
articles.body:
Matt Damon opened up about a health scare involving his wife, Luciana Damon.

The Oscar-winning actor revealed in a new interview with GQ , published on Thursday, that his wife underwent surgery for a brain aneurysm just one week before the 2024 Academy Awards .

"We had this whole scary thing happen where my wife had a brain aneurysm," Damon, 56, told the magazine. "She's totally fine, thank God, but [she] had this brain surgery the week before the Oscars."

"It was the first night she felt good enough to get up and had her energy back," he said.

A brain aneurysm occurs when a weakened area in the wall of an artery in the brain bulges outward and fills with blood, according to the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke.

Some brain aneurysms cause no symptoms, while others can rupture and cause bleeding in or around the brain, potentially leading to a stroke, brain damage or death, according to the agency.

Damon did not disclose whether his wife's aneurysm ruptured or provide additional details about her surgery.

Despite undergoing surgery just days earlier, Luciana surprised Damon by getting dressed up and joining him at an Oscars after-party, where his film "Oppenheimer" was being celebrated after winning seven awards, including best picture .

"And she surprised me and got a dress and we went out to the after-party, because she remembered that the last time it happened, I didn't do it," Damon recalled. "And she was like, 'This time we're going out.'"

The actor was referring to the 2007 Oscars, when he and Luciana watched from home as his film "The Departed" won four awards, including best picture and best director for Martin Scorsese.

"I remember I was shooting second unit for 'The Bourne Ultimatum' during that Oscars [where 'The Departed' won], so I didn't go," Damon recalled. "I was living in Miami at the time, and I had an infant."

Damon said he was so excited when Scorsese won that he began jumping up and down in his bedroom, only to realize moments later that he had missed an opportunity to celebrate in person.

"And I turned to Lucy and I was like, 'S---, we should be there!'" he recalled. "I totally blew it."

Reflecting on his wife's determination to celebrate with him nearly two decades later, Damon said, "And it was pretty f------ heroic of her to do that and really meaningful."

articles.title: Met Gala 2027: Exhibit to examine everyday items of clothing, replacing scuttled John Galliano show
articles.summary: And now, Take 2: The new Met Gala exhibit will celebrate everyday garments and materials like jeans and puffer jackets, paper and plastic - and how
articles.body: And now, Take 2: The new Met Gala exhibit will celebrate everyday garments and materials like jeans and puffer jackets, paper and plastic - and how fashion designers transform them.The new theme announced Thursday sounds about as far as can be imagined from the glittering, elaborate designs of John Galliano, the British designer who was originally the subject of the Met's fashion exhibit next spring - before that idea was scuttled amid an outcry over past antisemitic statements.The replacement show at the Met's Costume Institute, "extraORDINARY: Fashion and the Poetics of the Everyday," will be launched by the 2027 Met Gala, held traditionally on the first Monday in May. Using items in the museum's collection, as well as loans and acquisitions, the exhibit aims to explore "how designers rework familiar garments, everyday objects, and commonplace materials through craft, construction, material experimentation, and conceptual wit," the museum says.When the original exhibit was canceled, there was 'no Plan B'It is being assembled, as always, by the institute's head curator, Andrew Bolton. The idea had to come together quickly once the museum, along with Galliano himself, decided to cancel the scandal-plagued retrospective under pressure from donors, city officials and the Jewish community.In an interview this week, Bolton described the challenge of coming up with a new idea from scratch after the cancellation of the Galliano show, which he called a disappointment. The institute had already been collecting Galliano designs for the original show, which was announced with fanfare in late July. The museum had promised to directly confront, in the show, the designer's "derogatory conduct that fundamentally altered his career and public reception" - a reference to past antisemitic and racist statements. But a month later, the show was scrapped entirely."I had no Plan B, to be honest," Bolton said. "There wasn't another exhibition already researched and ready to go." He said the new idea had occurred to him while he was working on last year's show, "Costume Art," but had remained merely "a twinkle in my eye."But that twinkle, he said, "sort of led me to think more about how we experience clothing in everyday life, obviously through wearing it but (also) through memory and movement.""Everyday clothes carry extraordinary amounts of meaning," Bolton said. "We have a favorite T-shirt, we have a favorite pair of jeans, and we wear them until they literally fall apart. And those meanings develop through wearing."The show looks at how designers make these garments into something different and unique. "I like the idea that designers turn these familiar things into these incredible sources of wonder," he said.Bolton hopes people, after visiting the show, will look differently at the clothes they are wearing. In fact, he said, he was toying with the idea of suggesting a "dress code" to the general public, asking them to wear a favorite pair of jeans or T-shirt or bomber jacket."I think it'll make you think about what you're wearing," he said.There will be at least one pair of very famous jeansAbout a third of the show will consist of items in the museum's own collection, and the remaining items will be loans from design houses or gifts. One special loan, from London's Victoria and Albert Museum: An iconic puffer coat by designer Charles James, from the 1930s. Also in the puffer section will be a noted "sleeping bag coat" by designer Norma Kamali.A number of designers also will be contributing items in honor of the Costume Institute's 80th anniversary next year. "So we're using it as an opportunity to continue to diversify the collection," Bolton said.There's also a notable pair of jeans, which themselves generated a bit of controversy.Bolton said Brooke Shields has contributed the Calvin Klein jeans from her famous ad campaign - made when she was only 15 - in which she told the world that nothing came between her and her Calvins.The Met Gala's hosts and dress code will be announced at a later dateThe spring exhibit is launched each year by the starry Met Gala, a fundraiser for the museum's Costume Institute, where guests tour the show during cocktail hour. The most visible and photographed event on the fashion calendar is a much-coveted invite, drawing a mix of luminaries from the worlds of entertainment, business, sports and politics.The exhibit's theme influences the evening's dress code on the carpet, which will be announced at a later date - as will the newest slate of celebrity hosts for the May 3 gala.One of the foremost critics of the Galliano exhibit was a past attendee, New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin, who said she'd met many times with museum leaders to voice opposition. The gala would have, in 2027, fallen on Holocaust Remembrance Day. The daughter of a Holocaust survivor, Menin said in August that the cancellation was "the correct decision, as the harm and pain this was causing was simply unacceptable."Galliano, long recognized as one of the fashion world's biggest talents, spent years as creative director of Christian Dior. He was fired when a series of racist and antisemitic comments from 2010 and 2011 went viral, leading to his conviction in an antisemitism trial in France. Galliano spent several years involved in public and private efforts to make amends. He made a comeback in 2014 when he was hired by Paris fashion house Maison Margiela, where he remained for a decade."I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it," Galliano said in a statement when his exhibit was canceled.The gala is overseen by Anna Wintour, Vogue's global editorial director, one of the most influential figures in fashion and a longtime supporter of Galliano."John's decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is," Wintour said in an August statement.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.summary: Influencer infantil Jessica Sousa Borba chorou ao citar que Melody cancelou participação no evento porque estará no Festival Rock The Mountain. Pai da cantora desmente e diz que ela está com medo de voar.
articles.body:
Jessica Sousa Borba diz que Melody cancelou participação em sua festa de 15 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Nesta quinta-feira (05), a influencer infantil Jessica Sousa Borba apareceu aos prantos em seu Instagram questionando: "Quanto vale o meu sonho para você?".

Nas imagens, Jessica, que tem um canal no YouTube com mais de três milhões de assinantes e 1,5 milhão de seguidores no Instagram, segue o desabafo afirmando que, para a cantora Melody, seu sonho "não vale nada".

Melody seria uma das atrações da festa de 15 de anos de Jéssica, que acontece nesta sexta-feira (6), em Brasília. Mas cancelou sua participação.

"Simplesmente faltam 24 horas para a minha festa e ela falou que não vai vir mais na minha festa. Ela era a atração confirmada na minha festa e ela disse que não vai vir mais porque ela marcou outro show no mesmo dia", relatou Jessica no vídeo.

Melody é uma das atrações do Festival Rock The Mountain, no Rio de Janeiro. A cantora sobe ao palco às 20h, nesta sexta-feira (6).

Em seguida, sua mãe, Francisca Maria de Sousa, entra para dar mais detalhes do ocorrido:

"A gente tem esse contrato com a Melody já tem um ano. Simplesmente, o empresário dela que deve ser uma pessoa muito irresponsável, pegou outro show no mesmo dia do aniversário da Jessica. Aí agora ela liga pra falar que não vai vir, se eu não quero que ela venha no sábado aqui em casa", afirma Francisca.

"Eu não quero ela aqui em casa", gritam mãe e filha no vídeo.

"A gente contratou ela caro pra ela poder estar no aniversário da Jessica. A gente já passou por vários bocados com eles, já pagamos a mais do que estava no contrato pra contratar jatinho. E a desculpa dela hoje é que está com medo de entrar num jatinho. Isso é coisa de profissional?", questiona Francisca.

"Pra ela, é só um contrato. Mas pra mim, ela tá estragando com meu sonho", afirma Jéssica aos prantos, antes de a mãe pausar o vídeo.

A cantora Melody, sucesso com o hit “Jet Ski se apresenta em São José do Rio Preto (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

Segundo Thiago Abreu, o Belinho, pai e empresário de Melody, o show do Rock The Mountain não inviabiliza a participação de Melody na festa de Jessica.

Mas o empresário conta que, o que aconteceu, é que a cantora está com medo de voar e teve alguns pressentimentos.

"Nunca demos mancada em festa de ninguém. E aí, nesse dia, a gente tem outro compromisso, que é aqui no Rio, mas um não atrapalha o outro, porque ela está dizendo que a gente está cancelando a festa por causa de outro show. É mentira. A nossa festa aqui do Rio de Janeiro é 20h. A festa dela é 02h. Um não atrapalha o outro."

Belinho diz ainda que, "quando foi alugar jato, eu falei com a mãe da menina pra ver se ela conseguia ajudar com um pouco mais. Porque eu fechei esse show lá atrás muito barato. E tá tudo bem, combinado não sai caro. Pedi ajuda, ela ajudou com R$ 20 mil a mais. O jato é R$ 85 mil mais barato."

"Vou colocar do meu bolso, porque se juntar o cachê e os R$ 20 mil que ela ajudou, não dá o jato. Porque foi um cachê baixo. Vou gastar uns R$ 50 mil, R$ 60 mil do meu bolso, a gente vai fazer o show de graça", citou o empresário.

"Só que devido às circunstâncias de tempo, devido ao avião que caiu, as meninas começaram a ficar com medo. 'Pai, estou tendo pressentimento...' e começaram a ficar com ansiedade."

Belinho confirma que Melody entrou em contato com Jessica para explicar o cancelamento. "Ela falou que estava com medo e disse que, pelo o que a gente recebeu do pessoal que vai pilotar o jato, as condições não são boas. Eu sei da importância da sua festa, do seu aniversário, mas estou com medo de entrar no avião."

Segundo Belinho, um tio de Jessica entrou em contato para oferecer um avião maior. E, assim, eles disseram que iriam. "Enquanto ela postou o vídeo, eu e esse familiar estávamos fazendo com que o show acontecesse. Tenho as conversas aqui. Mas ao invés de tentar resolver a situação, ela simplesmente postou vídeo chorando na internet, falando que pagou o jato do bolso dela."

MC Daniel e MC Mirella se apresentam este final de semana em Ribeirão Preto, SP — Foto: Divulgação

Após desabafar no Instagram, Jessica recebeu diversas mensagens de artistas se disponibilizando para fazer a apresentação na festa. Entre eles, MC Daniel e MC Mirella.

"Se você quiser eu canto na sua festa e danço com você. Me passa as informações da sua festa no direct por favor, princesa", escreveu Daniel.

"Se quiser eu e minhas amigas vamos! Sei que não somos ela, mas sei lá! Estamos à disposição! Vai dar tudo certo. Melody é uma menina maravilhosa também, acho que vão tentar uma solução pra você, fica calma que dará tudo certo! Em nome de Jesus! De qualquer forma, torcendo aqui por você", escreveu Mirella.

"Chegou o grande dia da minha festa. Confesso que estou acabada, não imaginei que seria assim, não esperava isso. Mas Deus sabe de todas as coisas. E estou assim, mas com coração cheio de gratidão por pessoas que se mobilizaram e abraçaram toda essa situação. Cantores de longe, que se ofereceram pra vir, como o MC Daniel e a MC Mirella, eles vão estar aqui hoje na minha festa. Saíram de lá 4horas da manhã de ônibus. Estou muito grata, não tenho palavras pra agradecer" comentou Jessica na manhã desta sexta-feira (6), dia do evento.

articles.title: Turma do Pagode defende isenção política de artistas e comenta polêmica com Jorge e Mateus | G1
articles.standfirst: Caramelo e Leizinho debateram a pressão pelo posicionamento político nas redes sociais e comentaram a recente polêmica envolvendo dupla sertaneja.
articles.summary: Caramelo e Leizinho debateram a pressão pelo posicionamento político nas redes sociais e comentaram a recente polêmica envolvendo dupla sertaneja.
articles.body:
Caramelo e Leizinho, do grupo Turma do Pagode, participaram do podcast "g1 ouviu" e defenderam artistas que não se posicionam politicamente. Eles também comentaram os recentes cancelamentos de shows da dupla sertaneja Jorge & Mateus em capitais do Nordeste.

🔎 As prefeituras do Recife e de Fortaleza cancelaram os shows da dupla sertaneja após o cantor Jorge declarar apoio ao candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nas eleições de 2026.

Ao abordarem a pressão exercida pelo público sobre o posicionamento de artistas em anos eleitorais, Leizinho avaliou que a exigência representa uma invasão da vida pessoal e defendeu que o recolhimento é uma escolha legítima.

"Acho que nisso [de cobrar posicionamento] você acaba invadindo a vida pessoal da pessoa. A pessoa não é obrigada [a revelar] o partido dela", disse Leizinho, lembrando ter mantido seu "voto secreto" durante o período eleitoral para evitar confusão.

Turma do pagode no g1 Ouviu — Foto: Cadu Lando/g1

Caramelo concordou com o colega e ressaltou que o regime democrático assegura tanto o direito à manifestação quanto ao silêncio, mas fez questão de destacar que toda tomada de posição traz desdobramentos práticos.

"Se você quer expor, você tem direito. Se você não quer expor, você também tem direito. Você tem direito de fazer o que você quiser, só que tudo tem uma consequência", concluiu.

Dupla Jorge e Mateus — Foto: Cadu Fernandes

A polêmica com a dupla sertaneja começou após o cantor Jorge interpretar uma paródia do sucesso "Pode Chorar" com a frase "Pode chorar, mas eu não voto no PT".

Na noite de terça-feira (3), o prefeito do Recife, Victor Marques (PCdoB), anunciou o cancelamento da apresentação da dupla no Réveillon da cidade, marcada para 27 de dezembro.

O prefeito justificou o recuo na contratação e afirmou que "não há mais clima para a apresentação da dupla" em função das críticas nas redes sociais.

No mesmo dia, o prefeito de Fortaleza, Evandro Leitão (PT), comunicou a retirada dos sertanejos da programação de Ano-Novo da capital cearense, alegando "questões que geraram polêmicas".

Em sentido oposto, a Prefeitura de Salvador confirmou nesta quarta-feira (4) a dupla como uma das atrações do Festival Virada Salvador 2027.

O prefeito Bruno Reis (União Brasil) afirmou que convicções políticas não são critério para contratação de shows públicos. "Nós vivemos numa democracia, temos que respeitar as opiniões divergentes", disse.

Nas redes sociais, Jorge foi acusado de ter feito declarações xenofóbicas contra nordestinos, o que foi negado pelo cantor em nota oficial.

articles.title: Baco Exu do Blues envolve Marina Sena na aura sensual de 'Mon amour', single de latinidade 'caliente' que cita sucesso brega de Reginaldo Rossi no refrão | G1
articles.body:
Baco Exu do Blues e Marina Sena fazem feat inédito em 'Mon amour', primeiro single do rapper desde o álbum 'Hasos' (2025) — Foto: Divulgação

Artistas: Baco Exu do Blues & Marina Sena

♬ “Mon amour, meu bem, ma femme / Prometa nunca me largar / Mon amour, meu bem, ma femme / Tudo que eu amo sempre me abandona”. O refrão cantado por Baco Exu do Blues logo na introdução de “Mon amour” – single lançado pelo rapper às 21h de ontem, quinta-feira, 5 de novembro – explicita a referência à música “Mon amour, meu bem, ma femme” (Cleide, 1972), um dos maiores sucessos do cantor Reginaldo Rossi (1943 – 2013), ícone do brega pernambucano.

Primeiro feat de Baco Exu do Blues com a cantora mineira Marina Sena e primeiro lançamento fonográfico do artista baiano desde o álbum “Hasos” (2025), o single “Mon amour” é melódico e até flerta com a aura desbragadamente romântica do brega, mas em essência transita pelo universo do R&B pop e sensual com latinidade caliente .

Essa latinidade salta aos ouvidos na longa passagem instrumental que ocupa os dois minutos finais da gravação de quatro minutos e meio, feita sob direção musical de Marcelo de Lamare com produção de Dactes. É quando o single “Mon amour” se transmuta, perde o caráter melódico e ganha até um toque de jazz latino.

Contudo, até chegar essa parte instrumental, a gravação envolve Baco e Marina em atmosfera essencialmente sensual, sem o explícito teor erótico de músicas anteriores do rapper, mas a interação entre as vozes dos cantores é pouca. Cada intérprete canta sozinho a própria parte.

As vozes somente se encontram brevemente na repetição do refrão, momentos antes de “Mon amour” enveredar por outros caminhos a partir da já mencionada passagem instrumental que valoriza o single de Baco Exu do Blues com Marina Sena.

articles.summary: Estudantes de sete municípios estão entre os classificados da 11ª edição do Festival. A Grande Final será em 20 de dezembro, no Teatro Dom Bosco, com entrada gratuita.
articles.body:
Com idades entre 8 e 17 anos, estudantes de sete municípios de Mato Grosso do Sul e Mato Grosso tiveram 23 músicas selecionadas para a final do Festival de Música Autoral Estudantil (Fesmorena) 2026. As composições foram escolhidas por uma banca de jurados e mostram o talento de crianças e adolescentes dos dois estados.

A grande final será no dia 20 de dezembro, no Teatro Dom Bosco, em Campo Grande , com entrada gratuita. Das 23 músicas selecionadas, 16 concorrem na categoria Música Autoral Livre e sete na categoria especial Canção – 50 Anos de Mato Grosso do Sul.

Pela primeira vez, estudantes de Mato Grosso participam do festival. O estado terá cinco músicas na final, enquanto Mato Grosso do Sul será representado por 18 composições.

As músicas abordam temas como sentimentos, experiências pessoais e cultura regional, além de reunir diferentes estilos musicais.

As sete músicas da categoria especial abordam a história e a cultura de Mato Grosso do Sul, que completa 50 anos de criação em 2027.

Antes da final, os estudantes vão participar de atividades de preparação artística e produção audiovisual para melhorar as apresentações e trocar experiências com outros participantes.

O Fesmorena é realizado pelo Instituto Cerrado Central (ICC), com recursos do governo federal, por meio do Ministério da Cultura. O festival também tem parceria de comunicação com a TV Morena, em Mato Grosso do Sul, e a TV Centro América, em Mato Grosso.

articles.title: The New York Times reportedly in talks to buy Letterboxd for $330 million
articles.summary: Letterboxd, an online platform for movie lovers, has grown dramatically in recent years.
articles.body:
The New York Times Company has reportedly “entered exclusive negotiations” to acquire Letterboxd for $330 million, according to a report from The New York Times itself.

Letterboxd, an online platform for movie lovers that could be compared to Goodreads for movies, has grown dramatically in recent years. Letterboxd reported 3 million users in January 2021, a figure that grew to 28 million by April of this year. More than half of its users are under 35.

Letterboxd was previously reported to be seeking a new owner. According to the Times, film studios A24 and Sony were interested in the acquisition, but A24 was priced out.

Letterboxd is free, but users can access advanced features with a paid subscription. Its projected earnings for this year are estimated at $15 million, which is only about 4.5% of what the Times is supposedly offering to buy the company for.

The New York Times Company declined to comment on the acquisition to its own paper (lol). Personally, we wouldn’t be surprised if these anonymous tips were coming from inside the house, so we’re inclined to take this report pretty seriously.

articles.title: Brands lean into human creativity as handcrafted art becomes more of a luxury in the age of AI
articles.summary: Artists say brands are embracing traditional art forms and making a point to show off the human labor behind their campaigns.
articles.body: The sound of pencil putting lines to paper. The geometric shapes of a cartoon animal before it comes to life on the page. Those were the opening shots of a teaser for Prada’s 2026 holiday campaign, which introduced a series of films made “using the anachronistic craft of hand-drawn animation,” working with longtime Disney animator John Pomeroy. “I learned my craft with pencil and paper, old-school analog drawing with pencil and paper,” Pomeroy, who left Disney in 2003, says in the teaser video. It’s that kind of skill that some artists say has become a greater asset than ever. In the age of widespread and accessible AI, artists say they’ve noticed more brands leaning into handcrafted art as a selling point. In recent weeks, the luxury fashion houses Prada and Hermès touted their human-made art projects in social media campaigns — even tagging the artists behind the work to showcase their authenticity. Alina Golovlova, a stop-motion artist in Prague, said that recently, she has felt that her work is actually “appreciated more than in previous years” as brands try to separate themselves from the AI content flooding the internet. “In previous years, I felt like I was just some hired content creator. No one really cared to tag me or make a [collaborative post],” Golovlova said. “And I think now for brands, it becomes valuable to bring the artists together with the brand to show that they are working with real people.” Golovlova directed a short film for Anthropologie last month, featuring a needle-felted bunny, embroidered stars and stop-motion movements — all designed and put together entirely by hand by a team of artists. And the choice proved to be an effective marketing strategy, as support rolled in from commenters online. “Beautiful! Love the creativity and seeing something human made and NOT AI 👏❤️,” a user wrote on Anthropologie’s post, accruing thousands of likes. “AI = Broke, cheap, lazy,” another user posted in response to Prada’s campaign. “Art from human hands = High-end, luxurious, high quality.” Animator Jon Densk, who worked on the hand-drawn Prada campaign under Pomeroy, said that while he suspects AI still has a way to go before it can be used successfully in animation, he has seen signs of it in commercials. Coca-Cola, he said, comes to mind as a major company that has leaned into AI for its advertisements. “After the first one I saw two years ago, I was like, I’m not buying Coke until they stop it. I still haven’t bought a Coke in two years,” Densk said. “So having a stance against [AI], I think, is a smart move for brands.” Coca-Cola’s use of AI stirred some controversy, as attitudes about the technology remain divided over labor and environmental concerns, as well as fatigue over the swath of mass-produced content commonly described as “AI slop.” Still, Densk said he wasn’t expecting the explosion of support that Prada’s hand-drawn campaign would attract online. “I think people that see people like us who are still drawing things, and even people working in CG animation, as true craftsmen, because that stuff really does take hours and hours and hours of practicing to get to a proficient level,” Densk said. He said it’s nice to see a resurgence of appreciation for that craft, saying the response to Pomeroy’s project with Prada shows that a company is still rewarded when it puts money and time into individual human artists. French woodworker Thibaut Malet said he has also noticed more and more brands commissioning such work. Last month, Hermès approached him to create a miniature wooden reproduction of the flagship store at its historic Paris location. “During our initial discussions,” Malet wrote, “Hermès explained its approach to collaborating with artists and its commitment to defending craftsmanship, traditional know-how and métiers d’art in response to the growing influence of artificial intelligence.” His creation was showcased on the company’s social media pages, drawing support from many online who explicitly commented about their opposition to AI. Malet said that craftsmanship has always been associated with luxury and quality but that the arrival of AI will make the distinction between human-made creations and artificial production even more important as brands try to distinguish themselves. Yet some, like Densk, find it peculiar that handmade art could grow to be viewed as a “luxury.” “The funny thing about art is it’s so intrinsically human to do that. I mean, my daughter learned how to hold a pencil and make a line before she learned how to walk,” he said. “It’s something that you can do at any point in your life, whether it’s a little stick figure or a Monet painting.”

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Estate Drops Lawsuit Against Her Nephew as He Says He’s ‘Grateful to Put This Misunderstanding’ Behind Him
articles.summary: Seaver said in a statement through his attorney he was “grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him”
articles.body:
Dolly Parton's estate voluntarily dismissed its lawsuit against her nephew and former head of security Bryan Seaver

Seaver denied allegations that he made threats against Parton's business interests and said court filings disrupted his life

His mother Cassie Parton publicly defended their close relationship while mourning her sister

Dolly Parton 's estate is dropping its lawsuit against her nephew and former head of security Bryan Seaver.

She's Alive, LLC, a company Parton organized to tend to her business interests after her Aug. 25 death , filed a notice of voluntary dismissal of its lawsuit against Seaver in the Chancery Court of Tennessee on Thursday, Nov. 5, according to documents obtained by PEOPLE. The dismissal was filed without prejudice, meaning they could choose to file again.

The surprise filing comes after weeks of back and forth between She's Alive, which is operated by Parton's longtime manager Danny Nozell, and Seaver, who served as his aunt's head of security for more than 20 years before he was fired in September.

Attorneys for She's Alive and for Seaver did not immediately respond to PEOPLE's request for comment.

"Mr. Seaver cares deeply about his Aunt Dolly, her music, her family, and the incredible legacy she left behind," Seaver's attorney told TMZ in a statement. "He has made a career out of protecting his aunt while she was alive and remains committed to Dolly and his entire family. Mr. Seaver is grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him so that the entire family can continue to grieve peacefully and ensure that the bright light of Dolly's legacy remains entirely untouched."

She's Alive had alleged that Seaver made a number of extortionary threats that invoked his military background , and that his behavior had prompted the resignation of multiple employees. Seaver was also accused of threatening to "destroy" Parton's brand partnerships through a podcast.

He denied ever threatening anyone, and said his private messages with Nozell — in which he admitted to using "profane" language — were taken out of context in court documents. He maintained that their exchanges were "ultimately friendly," and said in an October court filing that She's Alive's temporary restraining order against him was interfering with his life and with his position as a beneficiary of Parton's trust.

"I care about Ms. Parton, her music, her legacy, and her family. I do not want this dispute to harm her legacy," he wrote in an Oct. 13 court filing.

A number of court hearings in the case were delayed and rescheduled, though a motion hearing was on the calendar for Nov. 13.

On Oct. 26, Seaver shared a lengthy message to his Facebook page written by his mother Cassie, who was country superstar Parton's younger sister. In the message, Cassie grieved her sibling and expressed her support for her son.

"In recent weeks, I have been asked to make a public statement concerning my son, Bryan Seaver. While I have struggled with the thought of speaking publicly during such a painful and personal time, I feel it is important that I share what is in my heart—not to address disagreements or disputes, but simply to speak as a mother who dearly loves her son," she wrote.

Cassie went on to describe the "very special and meaningful relationship" Seaver shared with the "Jolene" singer, who chose him to be the one to announce news of her death when the time came.

"I recognize that we are living through circumstances involving deeply personal matters, differing perspectives, and issues that deserve to be addressed thoughtfully, respectfully, and through the appropriate channels," she wrote. "My love for my son does not require me to publicly judge others, take sides in disagreements, or speak about matters that I may not fully understand. Nor should my silence on any particular issue ever be mistaken for a lack of love or concern for my child."

articles.summary: Kimmarie Johnson, famed actress from ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’, has passed away at the age of 50 after suffering a heart attack. Tributes pour in for the beloved actress known for her roles in film and television.
articles.body: Actress Kimmarie Johnson, who was best known for her appearance in ‘Beverly Hills, 90210,' has sadly passed away. She was 50.Kimmarie Johnson passes away at 50Johnson reportedly passed away in her home in Los Angeles after suffering a heart attack on October 27. However, TMZ reports that she passed away on November 4 after suffering complications from the attack.Her niece, Rhonda Scott, shared the news with the public and further shared that she had been taken to the nearby Cedars-Sinai Hospital. At the time, her doctors diagnosed her with a condition called “heart aneurysm condition.” Scott concluded that Kimmarie passed away peacefully in her home.According to Cleveland Clinic, a heart aneurysm, or aortic aneurysm, “is a bulge in the wall of your aorta, the main artery from your heart. Aortic aneurysms form in a weak area in your artery wall. They may rupture (burst) or split (dissect), which can cause life-threatening internal bleeding or block the flow of blood from your heart to various organs.”Tributes pour in for Kimmarie JohnsonNetizens shared their condolences for the ‘Dude, Where’s My Car?’ actress soon after the news of her passing was shared online. One person’s tweet on X (formerly known as Twitter) read, “Beautiful soul gone too soon," while actor Joey Gholam added, “I'm grateful I got the chance to know you and see you at the events all the time. You were amazing. I'm truly shocked and saddened by your passing. Praying for you and your family.” Another comment read, “My beautiful kimmie! I’m so sorry! You were a beautiful soul inside and out!! This is terrible!”, while many others shared heart emojis and dove emojis in the comment section of her last post on Instagram.Who was Kimmarie Johnson?Kimmarie Johnson was an American model, actress, beauty pageant titleholder, and businesswoman. Born on April 8, 1976, in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and had a degree in elementary education and child psychology from the California University of Pennsylvania. After getting her degree, she moved to New York City for better opportunities. She briefly worked as a flight attendant, which is where she was discovered by a modeling agency.She also won the Miss Pennsylvania USA pageant in 1992 and went on to compete in the 1993 Miss USA pageant, where she placed in the top five. She lived in LA to be closer to the Hollywood industry and started working in the acting industry. She featured in television shows such as ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ and 'V.I.P.,' along with films like ‘Dude, Where's My Car?’ and ‘Diary of a Tired Black Man.’She gave birth to her son, Cameron Nino, in 2003, after which she took a break for a few years to raise him and be there for him. articles.body: After months of speculation, fan theories and social media sleuthing, television actors and former Bigg Boss Kannada Season 11 contestants Aishwarya Shindogi and Shishir Shastry have made it official. The duo announced their engagement in a joint video recently, putting an end to relationship rumours.In the playful reel, the couple addressed the many labels fans had attached to their bond, from friendship and relationship to situationship. “To everyone wondering what ‘ship’ we are in — friendship, relationship, situationship, or Titanic ship — we aren’t in any of those. We are boarding the ship called life together,” they said, adding that #AISHIR was no longer just a hashtag. They also thanked those who had followed their journey, whether with speculation, trolling or genuine affection“Behind the speculations was a story. Behind the smiles was love. Behind the comments was your curiosity. Today, that story has a name — AISHIR,” read their caption, describing the engagement as the beginning of a lifetime together. The two first bonded inside the Bigg Boss house, where they became emotional anchors for each other. Their frequent public appearances after the show, temple visits across coastal Karnataka and collaborative ventures kept fans guessing about the nature of their relationship. Their recent pairing in the micro-series Rags to Rajakumari further fuelled the buzz.While they had earlier described themselves as close friends and business associates, their off-screen camaraderie continued to make them a favourite among fan pages. With the engagement announcement, the duo has now confirmed what many followers had long suspected. articles.title: Pedro Almodóvar, sobre Los Javis y 'La bola negra': "Es un hito lo que está ocurriendo"
articles.standfirst: El ojo clínico del cineasta en 'La Revuelta': "Es el gran fenómeno del cine español, yo creo que de los últimos veinte años"
articles.summary: El ojo clínico del cineasta en 'La Revuelta': "Es el gran fenómeno del cine español, yo creo que de los últimos veinte años"
articles.body: Pedro Almodóvar atraviesa un buen momento, pero más allá de sus éxitos ha mirado hacia otro lado. Ha estado presente en La Revuelta y ha hablado mucho de "La bola negra", la película de Javier Ambrossi y Javier Calvo que se ha convertido en uno de los grandes fenómenos cinematográficos del momento. El cineasta se deshacía en elogios. "Es un hito lo que está ocurriendo con la película", ha asegurado, antes de explicar por qué considera que su éxito va mucho más allá de las cifras de recaudación. Y el cineasta ha dejado su sello particular. "Es el gran fenómeno del cine español, yo creo que de los últimos veinte años", indicaba. Y añadía que este film ha logrado conectar con un público que llevaba tiempo alejándose de determinadas propuestas del cine nacional, según su entender. Pero no se quedó ahí. Almodóvar ha ido un poco más. Por ello, ha aprovechado su intervención para lanzar una crítica a algunas de las producciones que han dominado la taquilla española durante los últimos años. "Los grandes éxitos del cine español últimamente son de otras características. Son básicamente con actores de televisión, producidos por televisiones también, y tienen un tufo televisivo y, sobre todo, familiar", ha indicado al respecto. Almodóvar ha contrapuesto ese modelo de cine con la propuesta de Los Javis, que considera muy diferente de las fórmulas comerciales habituales. "Esto es lo opuesto a una comedia familiar", ha defendido, subrayando que la película aborda asuntos como la guerra y las dificultades de ser homosexual.

articles.title: Manu Sánchez sobre el 29-N y el auge de la ultraderecha: ¿Y si el mundo...?"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de 'El perro andaluz' se mete de lleno en cuestiones políticas
articles.summary: El presentador de 'El perro andaluz' se mete de lleno en cuestiones políticas
articles.body: El humorista Manu Sánchez ha tratado, en su monólogo del programa 'El Perro Andaluz' asuntos de actualidad política, mezclado con el humor y la reflexión. Pero en este caso, el asunto ha ido con mayor profundidad. Se ha centrado en cómo está España y en lo que pueda ocurrir en las elecciones generales del próximo 29 de noviembre. Y ha lanzado una advertencia. "¿Y si el mundo de repente ya estuviese cansado de este camino de autodestrucción y hubiese decidido ser un poquito, una mijita mejor?", señalaba el presentador. Sánchez ha planteado la posibilidad de que otros países estén comenzando a alejarse de determinados discursos extremistas mientras aquí se produce el movimiento contrario. "¿Y si el mundo necesitase volver a la tontería esa de la civilización, la educación y la humanidad?", ha preguntado, reivindicando la defensa de los servicios públicos, la sanidad, la educación y el Estado del bienestar. Y ha reflexionados especialmente en un asunto: en las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. "¿Y si al final todo cambia? ¿O al revés? ¿Y si no cambia nada? ¿O mejor? ¿Y si cambia a tiempo?", ha dejado entre preguntas. Sobre la posibilidad de que España llegue tarde a lo que ha denominado el "pendulazo" de la política internacional y termine avanzando en una dirección contraria a la que, según su interpretación, empiezan a tomar otros países. "Que España, una vez más, llegase tarde a este pendulazo que parece que ya está dando el reloj del fascismo mundial", ha señalado.

articles.body: ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ released in cinemas on November 5 amid high expectations, with its impressive advance booking figures raising hopes of a strong opening at the box office. The film, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi and Ravi Dubey, among others, opened at Rs 64.85 crore net in India on Day 1. While it surpassed the opening-day collection of Ranbir's previous release, ‘Animal’, it fell short of the record set by ‘Dhurandhar 2’, which had opened at Rs 102 crore net at the domestic box office.With the film entering its first weekend, expectations are high for a further jump in collections. Friday could see an improvement in footfalls, particularly during the evening and night shows, while the weekend holiday period is expected to bring in more audiences. Saturday and Sunday could prove crucial for the film as it looks to build on its opening-day momentum and maintain a strong run at the box office.On Day 2, the film has collected Rs 34.06 crore till afternoon, taking its Hindi version's contribution to Rs 20.65 crore. Despite Yash's presence in the film, the Kannada version has not witnessed the kind of traction that was expected, with the Hindi version continuing to account for the bulk of its collections.With these figures, the film's total domestic box office collection has reached Rs 98.91 crore net. The coming days will be important in determining whether ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ can capitalise on the weekend advantage and translate its strong opening into a sustained box office run. Its performance over the next two days will also offer a clearer indication of how audiences are responding to the film across markets.Day-wise box office collection of ‘Ramayana: Part 1’- Day 1: Rs 64.85 crore- Day 2 (LIVE): Rs 34.06 croreTotal collection: Rs 98.91 crore net in IndiaNote: Day 2 figures are live and subject to change as the day's shows progress.The film is directed by Nitesh Tiwari, best known for helming ‘Dangal’ and ‘Chhichhore’, and produced by Namit Malhotra. It features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Ram, Yash as Ravana, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The ensemble cast also includes Kajal Aggarwal, Arun Govil, Lara Dutta and Indira Krishnan, among others.
